::: {#ant-foraging-simulation .project-card}
## [Ant Foraging Simulation](https://github.com/tpace31){target="_blank"}

![](images/ants-preview.png){width=100% style="max-height: 250px; object-fit: cover; border-radius: 6px; margin-bottom: 1rem;"}

**Description:**  
An agent-based stochastic simulation investigating how localized interactions and pheromone gradient fields lead to optimal foraging routes and resource gathering efficiency.

<span class="skill-tag">Python</span>
<span class="skill-tag">Stochastic Modeling</span>
<span class="skill-tag">Differential Equations</span>
<span class="skill-tag">Simulation</span>

<details class="project-preview">
<summary>Preview Methodology & Equations</summary>

### Mathematical Formulation
Pheromone trail concentration $P(x, y, t)$ across the continuous spatial domain is modeled incorporating both diffusion and exponential decay:

$$\frac{\partial P}{\partial t} = D \nabla^2 P - \gamma P + S(x, y, t)$$

Where:
* $D$ is the spatial diffusion coefficient.
* $\gamma$ is the natural evaporation rate constant.
* $S(x, y, t)$ represents pheromone deposition by returning foragers.

[View Repository on GitHub $\rightarrow$](https://github.com/tpace31){.btn .btn-sm .btn-primary style="margin-top: 0.5rem;"}
</details>
:::

::: {#propofol-pharmacokinetics .project-card}
## [Propofol Clearance & Pharmacokinetics](https://github.com/tpace31){target="_blank"}

![](images/propofol-preview.png){width=100% style="max-height: 250px; object-fit: cover; border-radius: 6px; margin-bottom: 1rem;"}

**Description:**  
A three-compartment pharmacokinetic model evaluating the distribution, clearance kinetics, and dynamic equilibrium of propofol in central and peripheral tissue volumes during clinical infusion protocols.

<span class="skill-tag">Python</span>
<span class="skill-tag">R</span>
<span class="skill-tag">Pharmacokinetics</span>
<span class="skill-tag">ODEs</span>
<span class="skill-tag">Numerical Integration</span>

<details class="project-preview">
<summary>Preview Compartment Model</summary>

### System of Differential Equations
The rate of change of drug mass in the central compartment $x_1(t)$ and peripheral compartments $x_2(t), x_3(t)$ is expressed by:

$$\frac{dx_1}{dt} = I(t) - (k_{10} + k_{12} + k_{13})x_1 + k_{21}x_2 + k_{31}x_3$$

$$\frac{dx_2}{dt} = k_{12}x_1 - k_{21}x_2$$

$$\frac{dx_3}{dt} = k_{13}x_1 - k_{31}x_3$$

Where $I(t)$ is the input infusion rate and $k_{ij}$ are inter-compartmental micro-rate transfer constants.

[View Repository on GitHub $\rightarrow$](https://github.com/tpace31){.btn .btn-sm .btn-primary style="margin-top: 0.5rem;"}
</details>
:::
